title: Fixed Long Radial Arm and Cube Table Drill
description: One newly authored whole fixed floor radial-drilling-machine-inspired exterior. A whole long broad base carries one tall left cylindrical column and collar, a long complete horizontal arm and a separate full cube table under an offset front spindle. The complete geared-head appearance lies partway along the arm, with a full exposed quill, short blunt spindle nose, top motor exterior, three-spoke front feed control and side open handwheel. Two long front guide strips, a full column-side elevating screw appearance, upper drive exterior, lower/upper guides and blank controls belong to the same machine. The whole cube table has three genuine top-open and end-open T-section channels in one continuous solid body, not painted lines or loose rails. All numeric geometry newly authored; no bench drill, knee mill, radial robot, saw carriage or old table parts imported. Unlike the small rear-column bench drill with bored arm table and belt lid, this has an extensive floor base, tall lifting-collar column, far-reaching full arm with an offset head, and a separate complete cube-table body; unlike the knee mill it has no crossed saddle or knee-supported transverse table. One whole model zero scenes. Static empty art only: no drill bit, workpiece, actual boring, head travel, column swing, gear train, thread engagement, quill feed, guide fit, power, coolant, precision, load, manufacture, ergonomics or safety capability. No copied brand dimensions or performance. Rigging animation and interaction not made.
